`IndexToken` clone is deployed per portfolio by `IndexFactory`.      The clone is simultaneously the ERC20 share contract and the custody      vault for that portfolio's basket. All basket parameters are set once      at `initialize` and are thereafter immutable.      Security model highlights:        - CEI everywhere; `burn` computes payouts before burning shares, and          burns shares before transferring tokens.        - Delta-based accounting on `mint`: every slot's contribution is          measured via `balanceOf` before/after, so a lying adapter cannot          mint more shares than it actually delivered.        - First-mint safe share pricing: creator-only, MIN_SEED floor,          MIN_LIQUIDITY permanently locked to prevent share-price inflation          attacks.        - Subsequent-mint pricing uses `min_i (delta_i / balance_i)` so no          slot can dilute existing holders.        - `nonReentrant` on all mutating entrypoints. `SafeERC20` on every          token transfer. `Initializable` locks the implementation.      Accepted edge case \u2014 drained-basket DoS (M-4 in audit log):        If every share except the locked MIN_LIQUIDITY floor at DEAD is        burned, an async slot's `_asyncSlotBalance[i]` may settle at zero        while `totalSupply == MIN_LIQUIDITY > 0`. Subsequent `finalizeMint`        calls then enter the subsequent-mint path of        {BasketMath.minDilutionShares}, which reverts on `bBefore == 0`        for that slot. The basket is permanently un-mintable in that        state.        Treated as ABANDONED rather than buggy: the basket is empty by        definition, no user funds are at risk (the locked MIN_LIQUIDITY        is intentionally orphaned at DEAD), and the failure is loud        (clean revert, no silent bad state). Re-seeding via a special-        case path was rejected because it would weaken the inflation-        attack defense for a rare, value-of-zero condition. allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

balanceOf(address).details: Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.

balances().details: Returns the *available* basket balance per slot — i.e. live ERC20      balance with per-token sync escrow and per-token funding-leftover      escrow subtracted (sync slots), or the virtual attested balance      tracked off-chain custody (async slots). Pending async intents      therefore do not inflate `balances()` and consequently cannot      dilute existing share holders.

burn(uint256,uint256[]).details: Reverts with {IndexToken_BasketHasAsyncSlot} if any slot is async;      use {burnAsync} for those baskets.

params.minAmountsOut: Per-slot floor; revert if any slot returns strictly less.
params.shares: Amount of share tokens to burn (held by caller).

burnAsync(uint256,uint256[],bytes[]).details: Required for any basket containing at least one async slot;      sync-only baskets MUST use {burn}.

params.minAmountsOut: Per-slot floor; revert if any slot returns strictly less.
params.nativeRecipients: Per-slot native-chain recipient bytes; length ==        tokens.length. For sync slots the entry is ignored (MUST be        empty); for async slots it MUST be non-empty.
params.shares: Amount of share tokens to burn (held by caller).

cancelMint(bytes32).details: Strict CEI: every state mutation (resolved flag + escrow        decrements) happens BEFORE any external call (sync ERC20        refunds, async-adapter cancel signals, queue mark-cancelled).        `markCancelled` itself enforces the queue-side deadline check;        moving it to the end means a not-yet-expired intent reverts        the entire transaction atomically, undoing the state writes        and refund transfers above. The ERC20 + adapter calls inside        this function carry their own `wake-disable-next-line`        directives where applicable; with this CEI ordering, none of        those calls observe in-progress state.

constructor.details: Initializes the implementation with empty name/symbol (clones supply      their own via `initialize`) and permanently locks the implementation      against direct initialization.      ETH-lock note (intentional): this contract is `payable` only via      `mint`, and there is no `receive` / `fallback`. Any non-mint ETH      send reverts. Inside `mint`, `msg.value` is required to equal      `amountIn` exactly and is wrapped to WETH in the same call, so      no ETH ever rests in the contract. The contract intentionally      has NO ETH withdrawal function: any `selfdestruct`-forced ETH      is unrecoverable but harmless to user funds (vault holdings are      ERC20 tokens). Adding a withdraw function would create a worse      attack surface (admin trust, share-holder dilution, etc.) for      no defensible benefit.

params.weth_: Canonical WETH9 address for this chain.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

finalizeMint(bytes32,uint256).details: Reverts if `block.timestamp > a.intentDeadline`. Once the      deadline elapses the intent's only legitimate exit is      `cancelMint`. This is a deliberate lock-down (versus allowing      either-finalize-or-cancel after the deadline): the user signed      up for refund-on-timeout when they set the deadline; honoring      that intent on-chain is preferable to a tx-ordering race      between keeper finalize and user cancel.

params.minSharesOut: Slippage floor measured at finalize time.

returns.sharesOut: Shares minted to the originator (excluding any         first-mint floor permanently locked at `DEAD`).

getAsyncIntent(bytes32).details: Returns zero values for unknown intents (no revert; callers      should rely on `exists` to distinguish absent intents from      resolved-but-purged ones).

initialize((address[],uint16[],address[].details: Validation pipeline:        1. {_validateInitInvariants}: length equality, slot-count           range, non-empty name/symbol, non-zero creator, no zero           addresses in `tokens`/`adapters`, no duplicates, async           detection. Returns `anyAsync` so the queue-presence check           does not need to re-scan.        2. IntentQueue presence/absence check (must match `anyAsync`).        3. {BasketMath.validateWeights}: weights sum to {BasketMath.BPS},           none zero.      The factory verifies each adapter's `assetForm` BEFORE cloning,      so this function makes ZERO external calls — strict CEI on      every initializer.

mint(address,uint256,uint256,uint256,byt.details: Known griefing-style limitation (not exploitable for theft): an      attacker can front-run a mint by donating one of the basket      tokens directly to the vault, inflating `balancesBefore[i]` for      that slot. Because subsequent-mint share pricing uses      `min_i (delta_i * supply / balanceBefore_i)`, the inflated      denominator produces fewer `sharesOut`. The victim does not lose      funds — `minSharesOut` reverts the mint and refunds the input      atomically — but the gas is wasted, and the attacker pays the      donation amount with no direct gain. Frontends MUST quote a      realistic `minSharesOut` (e.g., 99.5% of the on-chain estimate)      so honest market drift does not also revert. There is no      contract-level mitigation that doesn't introduce a worse      attack surface (e.g., trusting external price oracles).

params.amountIn: Total amount of `fundingToken` the caller supplies.
params.deadline: Unix seconds after which the call reverts unexecuted.
params.fundingToken: ERC20 the caller is paying with (must be factory-allowlisted).
params.minSharesOut: Revert if fewer shares than this would be minted.
params.perSlotHints: Per-slot opaque routing data, length == tokens.length.

returns.sharesOut: Number of shares minted to the caller.

mintAsync(address,uint256,uint64,bytes[].details: Pulls `amountIn` of `fundingToken` from `msg.sender`, dispatches every      sync slot via its adapter (delivered ERC20 escrowed against this      intent), dispatches every async slot via its adapter (funding sent      to the partner network), and records the intent in the      {IIntentQueue}. Shares are NOT minted here — call {finalizeMint}      after the {AttestationOracle} has attested every async slot.

params.amountIn: Total amount of `fundingToken` the caller supplies.
params.fundingToken: ERC20 the caller is paying with (must be allowlisted).
params.intentDeadline: Unix seconds; oracle must attest before this.
params.perSlotHints: Per-slot adapter routing data; length == tokens.length.

returns.intentId: The {IIntentQueue} id for the new mint intent.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

burnAsync(uint256,uint256[],bytes[]).notice: Burns `shares` and dispatches per-slot pro-rata payouts.         Sync slots transfer ERC20 in-tx; async slots invoke the         adapter's `redeemAsync` and emit a withdrawal intent.

 @dev Initializes the implementation with empty name/symbol (clones supply

      ETH-lock note (intentional): this contract is `payable` only via
      `mint`, and there is no `receive` / `fallback`. Any non-mint ETH
      send reverts. Inside `mint`, `msg.value` is required to equal
      `amountIn` exactly and is wrapped to WETH in the same call, so
      no ETH ever rests in the contract. The contract intentionally
      has NO ETH withdrawal function: any `selfdestruct`-forced ETH
      is unrecoverable but harmless to user funds (vault holdings are
      ERC20 tokens). Adding a withdraw function would create a worse
      attack surface (admin trust, share-holder dilution, etc.) for
      no defensible benefit.

@inheritdoc IIndexToken
 @dev Known griefing-style limitation (not exploitable for theft): an
      attacker can front-run a mint by donating one of the basket
      tokens directly to the vault, inflating `balancesBefore[i]` for
      that slot. Because subsequent-mint share pricing uses
      `min_i (delta_i * supply / balanceBefore_i)`, the inflated
      denominator produces fewer `sharesOut`. The victim does not lose
      funds — `minSharesOut` reverts the mint and refunds the input
      atomically — but the gas is wasted, and the attacker pays the
      donation amount with no direct gain. Frontends MUST quote a
      realistic `minSharesOut` (e.g., 99.5% of the on-chain estimate)
      so honest market drift does not also revert. There is no
      contract-level mitigation that doesn't introduce a worse
      attack surface (e.g., trusting external price oracles).

@dev Snapshots each slot's basket-token balance BEFORE any funding pull
      or adapter interaction. Must run before `_pullFunding` so the
      funding-token slot's delta later equals the new allocation, not
      the entire pull amount.

@dev Transfers `L.amountIn` of `L.fundingToken` from `msg.sender` (or
      wraps `msg.value` if the funding token is WETH). Strict
      `msg.value == amountIn` check prevents stuck ETH; `msg.value == 0`
      check on the ERC20 path prevents accidentally swallowed ETH.

@dev Dispatches each slot's allocation through its adapter, measures
      delivery via balance delta, and asserts the funding-token balance
      dropped by exactly the total allocation we sent.
      Security model for the external `acquire` calls in the loop:
        1) `nonReentrant` on `mint` blocks cross-function re-entry.
        2) Push-only `safeTransfer` — adapters cannot pull extra funds.
        3) Per-slot delta check reverts before subsequent dispatches.
        4) Post-loop funding-balance sanity check.
        5) Strict CEI on share `_mint` (only after all checks pass).

@dev Computes the new share count from the validated `L.deltas` and
      `L.balancesBefore`. First-mint path: creator-only seed,
      `sqrt(amountIn * SHARE_SCALE)` shares with `MIN_LIQUIDITY` locked
      at `DEAD`. Subsequent-mint path: `min_i (delta_i * supply / balanceBefore_i)`
      so no slot can dilute existing holders.

      (`finalizeMint`, `cancelMint`, `burnAsync`, `burn`) is also
      `nonReentrant` and checks `_asyncIntents[id].exists` before

      functions revert on the unknown intent. True CEI would
      require IntentQueue to accept an externally-predicted id,
      a worse API trade-off than this controlled suppression.

 @dev Reverts if `block.timestamp > a.intentDeadline`. Once the
      deadline elapses the intent's only legitimate exit is
      `cancelMint`. This is a deliberate lock-down (versus allowing
      either-finalize-or-cancel after the deadline): the user signed
      up for refund-on-timeout when they set the deadline; honoring
      that intent on-chain is preferable to a tx-ordering race
      between keeper finalize and user cancel.

@title IndexToken
 @notice ERC20 share token + vault for a single Xindex portfolio.
 @dev One `IndexToken` clone is deployed per portfolio by `IndexFactory`.
      The clone is simultaneously the ERC20 share contract and the custody
      vault for that portfolio's basket. All basket parameters are set once
      at `initialize` and are thereafter immutable.
      Security model highlights:
        - CEI everywhere; `burn` computes payouts before burning shares, and
          burns shares before transferring tokens.
        - Delta-based accounting on `mint`: every slot's contribution is
          measured via `balanceOf` before/after, so a lying adapter cannot
          mint more shares than it actually delivered.
        - First-mint safe share pricing: creator-only, MIN_SEED floor,
          MIN_LIQUIDITY permanently locked to prevent share-price inflation
          attacks.
        - Subsequent-mint pricing uses `min_i (delta_i / balance_i)` so no
          slot can dilute existing holders.
        - `nonReentrant` on all mutating entrypoints. `SafeERC20` on every
          token transfer. `Initializable` locks the implementation.
      Accepted edge case — drained-basket DoS (M-4 in audit log):
        If every share except the locked MIN_LIQUIDITY floor at DEAD is
        burned, an async slot's `_asyncSlotBalance[i]` may settle at zero
        while `totalSupply == MIN_LIQUIDITY > 0`. Subsequent `finalizeMint`
        calls then enter the subsequent-mint path of
        {BasketMath.minDilutionShares}, which reverts on `bBefore == 0`
        for that slot. The basket is permanently un-mintable in that
        state.
        Treated as ABANDONED rather than buggy: the basket is empty by
        definition, no user funds are at risk (the locked MIN_LIQUIDITY
        is intentionally orphaned at DEAD), and the failure is loud
        (clean revert, no silent bad state). Re-seeding via a special-
        case path was rejected because it would weaken the inflation-
        attack defense for a rare, value-of-zero condition. Operationally:
        users move to a fresh portfolio.
